newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan steelmakers optimistic about 1997/98 profits.
newsitem.headline: Japan steelmakers optimistic about 1997/98 profits.

text.p: Japan's big steelmakers said on Thursday that their current profits may rise slightly in the next business year because of cost cutting and the weaker yen.
The five top steelmakers, except Kobe Steel Ltd, also predicted their profits for this fiscal year to March 31 would be higher than actual 1995/96 profits.

"We are targetting parent current profit of more than 100 billion yen for next year. Lower interest rates and the weak yen will help us achieve the target," Nippon Steel Corp managing director Takeshi Yoshii told reporters on Thursday.

NKK Corp revised down its 1996/97 profit forecast on poor sales of electronic devices, low orders received at its engineering division and weak steel prices. But a company official said the company still expects its 1997/98 profits to be the same or above the level reached this fiscal year.
NKK plans to cut crude steel output in 1997/98, which could also help improve the currently stagnant steel market, he said.
Kawasaki Steel Corp said it aims to post a parent current profit of around 30 billion yen in 1997/98, mainly as a result of cost-cutting efforts.
Kobe Steel Ltd, meanwhile, said it aims to post a parent current profit of more than 30 billion yen in 1997/98.
The steelmakers on average estimated Japan's overall crude steel output in 1997/98 at around 99 million tonnes against this year's level of about or slightly above 100 million.
